## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as

link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use

which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Neymar one-on-one football game for phones and tablets, including an intro cinematic, rival, stadium, dialogue, sound, and a slow-motion sombrero move.

## Requirements
- Realistic-looking 3D, recognizable Neymar in football kit with natural animations, professional stadium lighting, animated crowd, and cinematic camera.
- Playable throughout the X1, not just an animation; include character dialogue, crowd/narrator/kick sounds, and a cinematic intro.
- On victory, Neymar celebrates with Mavi and her father and conveys that he did it to protect her.
- Trigger a dramatic slow-motion scene when Neymar performs a sombrero on the arrogant rival.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a fresh Three.js/Vite browser game; synthesized audio avoids reliance on sound asset files.
- Assumed keyboard controls plus on-screen mobile joystick and action buttons.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Vite project setup in `package.json` and initial game UI in `index.html`.
- Added responsive HUD, intro, dialogue, mobile controls, and end-screen styling in `src/style.css`.
- Installed dependencies; `npm run build` passed before the game script was accidentally overwritten.

### Active
- Rebuilding `src/main.js` in chunks after an accidental overwrite. It currently has the Three.js renderer, stadium/pitch/crowd, player rig builder, and Neymar/rival initialization.
- Need finish gameplay, input, audio, dialogue, intro, slow-motion sombrero, goal logic, camera, animation loop, and test build/browser.

### Blocked
- Current `src/main.js` is incomplete; the game cannot run yet.

## Next Move
1. Continue `src/main.js` by adding ball, input, audio, match state/UI, gameplay, goals, camera, and render loop.
2. Run `npm run build`, fix errors, and browser-test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; ensure Neymar’s victory scene includes Mavi and her father.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and required HUD/intro/control elements.
- `src/main.js`: Partially rebuilt game implementation; currently incomplete.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `package.json`: Vite and Three.js dependencies/scripts.

## Important Context
- Earlier `src/main.js` was overwritten with only its final render-loop lines; it has since been restored partially through edits.
- The implemented victory copy currently mentions “vocês” but Mavi and her father are not yet represented as characters.

- Build a complete, playable 3D Neymar one-on-one football game for phones and tablets, including a cinematic intro, rival, stadium, dialogue, sound, and a slow-motion sombrero move.
- On victory, show Neymar celebrating with Mavi and her father and making clear he played to protect her.

## Requirements
- Realistic-looking 3D, recognizable Neymar in football kit with natural animations, professional stadium lighting, animated crowd, and cinematic camera.
- Playable throughout the X1, with character dialogue, crowd/narrator/kick sounds, and a cinematic intro.
- Slow-motion scene when Neymar performs a sombrero on the arrogant rival.
- Phone/tablet support and touch controls.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a Three.js/Vite browser game.
- Synthesized audio avoids relying on sound asset files.
- Supports keyboard controls plus an on-screen mobile joystick and action buttons.

### Completed
- Added Vite project setup in `package.json` and game UI in `index.html`.
- Added responsive HUD, intro, dialogue, mobile controls, and end-screen styling in `src/style.css`.
- Rebuilt substantial parts of `src/main.js`: Three.js stadium and pitch, player rigs, ball, keyboard/touch input, synthesized audio, intro/dialogue, gameplay, shots, scoring, and sombrero logic.

- Finish and validate `src/main.js`; the latest edits added the gameplay update function, but the render loop, resize handler, and final camera setup have not yet been restored.
- Run `npm run build`, fix issues, and browser-test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay.
- Add Mavi and her father as visible characters in the victory scene; the current end copy only mentions them.

### Blocked
- The game is not yet runnable: `src/main.js` is incomplete and has not been rebuilt or tested after the latest reconstruction.

1. Finish `src/main.js` with the animation/render loop, resize handling, blur cleanup, and initial camera framing.
2. Run `npm run build`; repair any syntax or runtime errors, then test the intro, movement, shooting, scoring, and sombrero.

- `index.html`: Game UI and required HUD, intro, controls, and end-screen elements.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

- An earlier accidental overwrite left `src/main.js` with only its final lines; reconstruction is ongoing.
- A build passed before that overwrite, but it does not validate the current script.
- Changes are uncommitted.
